site.name: Vernissage
site.tagline: A salon for tracking visual art with the ceremony of a gilded opening night.
site.intro: Catalog artworks, artists, exhibitions, and museum visits in a social review space shaped like a hand-bound exhibition catalogue.

movements.name: Impressionism
movements.description: Painting centered on changing light, atmosphere, season, and the sensation of seeing a scene in time.

movements.name: Post-Impressionism
movements.description: Building on Impressionism with bolder color, geometric structure, and personal vision — from pointillism to expressive brushwork.

movements.name: Art Nouveau
movements.description: Botanical linework, feminine silhouettes, and whiplash curves threaded through print and interior design.

movements.name: Symbolism
movements.description: Dreamlike, emotionally charged imagery rooted in allegory and atmosphere.

movements.name: Contemporary Photography
movements.description: Camera-based work centered on travel, documentary attention, landscape light, and the visual argument of the photograph.

movements.name: Pop Art
movements.description: Bright, graphic art shaped by advertising, leisure culture, bold flat color, and the visual speed of modern life.

movements.name: Abstract Art
movements.description: Painting that leaves literal depiction behind in favor of geometry, rhythm, color fields, and spiritual or perceptual structure.

movements.name: Performance Art
movements.description: Live, durational, or participatory art where the body, audience, and event become the medium.

movements.name: Architecture
movements.description: Built form treated as cultural authorship, where structure, circulation, ornament, and public space carry the work's meaning.

movements.name: Romanticism
movements.description: Art shaped by drama, feeling, sublime nature, and heightened narrative tension.

movements.name: Contemporary Digital Art
movements.description: Born-digital images that use software, concept-art workflows, and contemporary screen culture to build new pictorial worlds.

movements.name: Contemporary Realism
movements.description: Recent painting that keeps representational surfaces intact while pushing atmosphere, allegory, or social commentary through recognizable scenes.

movements.name: Contemporary Impressionism
movements.description: Modern painting that revisits broken color, shifting light, and tactile brushwork through present-day subjects and palettes.

movements.name: Surrealism
movements.description: Dream logic, psychic intensity, and unstable symbolic images staged with eerie conviction.

movements.name: Northern Renaissance
movements.description: Detailed, symbol-heavy painting from northern Europe, often charged with moral allegory, devotional drama, and imaginative invention.

movements.name: Rococo
movements.description: Elegant 18th-century art of ornament, surface pleasure, decorative wit, and refined domestic spectacle.

movements.name: Renaissance
movements.description: Painting shaped by reborn classicism, perspective, devotional intensity, and the new prestige of observation.

movements.name: Baroque
movements.description: Art of theatrical light, bodily drama, and high emotional stakes staged with force and immediacy.

movements.name: Ukiyo-e
movements.description: Japanese woodblock print culture centered on seasons, travel, actors, courtesans, and the fleeting theater of daily life.

movements.name: Fauvism
movements.description: Color-first modernism that uses bold, liberated hues to make structure and sensation arrive at once.

movements.name: Cubism
movements.description: Modernist fracture of form into shifting facets, planes, and simultaneous viewpoints.

movements.name: Realism
movements.description: Art that keeps ordinary places, people, and objects legible while pressing hard on mood, labor, or social fact.

movements.name: Photography
movements.description: Lens-based images treated as authored works of witness, sequence, framing, and tonal decision.

movements.name: Mexican Modernism
movements.description: Modern art shaped by revolutionary politics, indigenous memory, folk symbolism, and a forceful national visual language.

venues.name: Art Institute of Chicago
venues.description: One of the oldest and largest art museums in the United States, home to an encyclopedic collection spanning 5,000 years.

venues.name: Musée d'Orsay
venues.description: Housed in a former railway station, the Musée d'Orsay contains the world's finest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces.

artists.name: Claude Monet
artists.portraitLabel: Serial views of water, weather, and changing light
artists.bio: Claude Monet returned to the same ponds, grain stacks, riverbanks, and coastal paths again and again so that weather and time of day could become the true subject of the painting. His late works flatten space into atmosphere, while the earlier landscapes keep one foot in observation and the other in sensation.

artists.name: Vincent van Gogh
artists.portraitLabel: Post-Impressionist visionary
artists.bio: A Dutch painter whose bold colors and emotional brushwork transformed landscapes, still lifes, and portraits into deeply personal expressions. His prolific output during a decade of painting produced some of the most recognized works in Western art.

artists.name: Georges Seurat
artists.portraitLabel: Pioneer of pointillism
artists.bio: A French artist who pioneered chromoluminarism and pointillism — building images from tiny dots of pure color that optically blend at a distance. His monumental canvases brought scientific rigor to Impressionist color theory.

artists.name: Mary Cassatt
artists.portraitLabel: Chronicler of intimate life
artists.bio: An American painter and printmaker who became a central figure in French Impressionism. Known for tender depictions of mothers and children, domestic interiors, and Japanese-influenced compositions.

artists.name: Ken Rockwell
artists.portraitLabel: Technical evangelist of travel and landscape photography
artists.bio: Ken Rockwell turns road trips, desert light, and camera lore into cheerful photographic essays that hover between gear obsession and plein-air seeing.

artists.name: Matthew T. Rader
artists.portraitLabel: Open-license travel and documentary photographer
artists.bio: Matthew T. Rader publishes wide-ranging travel and documentary photographs under open licenses, moving from desert plants to weather damage and beach scenes with an eye for place.

artists.name: Hiroshi Nagai
artists.portraitLabel: City Pop dreamscapes in tropical flat color
artists.bio: Hiroshi Nagai distilled palm trees, hotel pools, and coastal highways into the languid visual grammar of City Pop, turning leisure architecture into a neon daydream.

artists.name: David Hockney
artists.portraitLabel: Pop scenes of pools, patios, and graphic flatness
artists.bio: David Hockney made California pools and domestic interiors feel as crisp as signage, flattening space into bright theatrical planes without losing the wit of observation.

artists.name: Max Cole
artists.portraitLabel: Minimalist fields of hand-drawn, meditative line
artists.bio: Max Cole builds paintings out of repeated, nearly breathing bands of line, letting tiny variations in touch turn restraint into a contemplative event.

artists.name: Marina Abramović
artists.portraitLabel: Durational performance built from endurance and attention
artists.bio: Marina Abramović uses stillness, repetition, and bodily risk to make presence itself feel sculptural, turning documentation into the public residue of performance.

artists.name: Richard Rogers
artists.portraitLabel: High-tech architecture with services turned outside out
artists.bio: Richard Rogers exposed lifts, ducts, and structure until buildings read like public diagrams, making infrastructure part of the spectacle.

artists.name: Edwin Landseer
artists.portraitLabel: Victorian animal portraitist of nobility, grief, and fur
artists.bio: Sir Edwin Landseer painted stags, hounds, and game birds with the psychological specificity Victorian portraiture usually reserved for humans.

artists.name: Jakub Różalski
artists.portraitLabel: Dieselpunk tableaux where mechs haunt rural fields
artists.bio: Jakub Różalski overlays mud, uniforms, and harvest-time villages with looming machines, giving alternate history the surface of a 19th-century painting.

artists.name: Simon Stålenhag
artists.portraitLabel: Retrofuturist melancholy in suburbs and fields
artists.bio: Simon Stålenhag stages rusting robots and impossible machinery against ordinary roads, lakes, and housing blocks, making sci-fi feel remembered instead of predicted.

artists.name: Bo Bartlett
artists.portraitLabel: American realism stretched toward allegory
artists.bio: Bo Bartlett paints family, ritual, and national myth at a cinematic scale, keeping realist surfaces while bending the scenes toward fable.

artists.name: Zdzisław Beksiński
artists.portraitLabel: Nightmare architecture and bone-dry apocalypse
artists.bio: Zdzisław Beksiński filled wastelands and interiors with eroded flesh, brittle arches, and funereal heat, making horror feel ceremonial rather than explosive.

artists.name: Thomas Kinkade
artists.portraitLabel: Luminous cottages and branded comfort-scapes
artists.bio: Thomas Kinkade turned cottages, chapels, and garden paths into engineered warmth, bathing every surface in a glow designed to feel instantly hospitable.

artists.name: Hilma af Klint
artists.portraitLabel: Mystical abstractions built from diagrams, petals, and force fields
artists.bio: Hilma af Klint treated painting like spiritual notation, layering spirals, petals, letters, and color systems into abstractions decades ahead of the canonical modernists.

artists.name: Alex Schaefer
artists.portraitLabel: Activist plein-air scenes with burning financial facades
artists.bio: Alex Schaefer folds protest into landscape painting, using brushy architecture and flames to turn banks and storefronts into arguments about power, debt, and spectacle.

artists.name: Hieronymus Bosch
artists.portraitLabel: Renaissance triptychs crowded with punishments and delights
artists.bio: Hieronymus Bosch packed paradise, temptation, and damnation into panoramic inventions where every hybrid creature seems to invent a new moral panic.

artists.name: Jean-Jacques Bachelier
artists.portraitLabel: Rococo painter of animals, flowers, and ornamental grace
artists.bio: Jean-Jacques Bachelier moved between pet portraiture, flowers, and decorative design, treating fur, petals, and porcelain surfaces as occasions for elegant display.

artists.name: Paul Signac
artists.portraitLabel: Pointillist harbors, rivers, and chromatic drift
artists.bio: Paul Signac translated rivers, ports, and coastal air into patient divisions of color, letting geometry and atmosphere arrive through dots and prismatic touches.

artists.name: Alena Aenami
artists.portraitLabel: Color-saturated digital worlds of mist and neon weather
artists.bio: Alena Aenami builds luminous fantasy and sci-fi environments from mist, reflections, and giant color chords, pushing digital landscape painting toward dream architecture.

artists.name: Jason Anderson
artists.portraitLabel: Palette-knife mosaics that push landscape toward abstraction
artists.bio: Jason Anderson treats coasts, skylines, and bridges as stained-glass weather systems, stacking thick shards of oil color until the scene flickers like reflected light.

artists.name: Jan van Eyck
artists.portraitLabel: Northern precision in oil, fur, glass, and prayer
artists.bio: Jan van Eyck made oil painting feel microscopically alert, turning jewels, reflections, and skin into arguments for painting as a technology of attention.

artists.name: Sandro Botticelli
artists.portraitLabel: Renaissance line, grace, and myth made airy
artists.bio: Botticelli lets line do nearly everything: hair, drapery, shells, and bodies drift with a decorative lightness that keeps mythology poised between dream and design.

artists.name: Caravaggio
artists.portraitLabel: Sacred drama lit like an ambush
artists.bio: Caravaggio pushed holiness and violence into the same beam of light, making revelation feel sudden, physical, and a little dangerous.

artists.name: Artemisia Gentileschi
artists.portraitLabel: Baroque heroines with real force behind the gesture
artists.bio: Artemisia Gentileschi paints biblical and classical women as agents rather than ornaments, giving their resolve and strain a muscular weight.

artists.name: Rembrandt
artists.portraitLabel: Light used as memory, psychology, and weather
artists.bio: Rembrandt can make a face, sleeve, or shadow feel newly discovered mid-painting, using light less as spotlight than as a slow form of thinking.

artists.name: Johannes Vermeer
artists.portraitLabel: Room-scale quiet built from light and delay
artists.bio: Vermeer turns domestic interiors into chambers of suspended attention, where a glance, letter, or instrument is enough to organize the entire room.

artists.name: Francisco Goya
artists.portraitLabel: Court elegance cracked open by nightmare and war
artists.bio: Goya can move from aristocratic polish to psychic ruin without changing painters, making satire, violence, and dread feel like parts of the same historical record.

artists.name: J. M. W. Turner
artists.portraitLabel: Storm, steam, and light dissolved to atmosphere
artists.bio: Turner paints weather as if it were the true subject of history, letting ships, cities, and mountains nearly disappear into radiant turbulence.

artists.name: Caspar David Friedrich
artists.portraitLabel: The sublime staged as solitude and horizon
artists.bio: Friedrich makes cliffs, fog, crosses, and winter trees feel like spiritual instruments, asking landscape to carry the full burden of thought.

artists.name: Katsushika Hokusai
artists.portraitLabel: Woodblock movement from wave-crash to mountaintop
artists.bio: Hokusai made line feel weather-fast and restless, moving from towering surf to compressed views of Mount Fuji with unmatched graphic economy.

artists.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
artists.portraitLabel: Travel print poetry in rain, snow, and season
artists.bio: Hiroshige turns roads, bridges, and showers of rain into compositional events, making travel itself feel like a shifting register of weather and mood.

artists.name: Gustav Klimt
artists.portraitLabel: Gold-ground intimacy between ornament and desire
artists.bio: Klimt lets bodies emerge from fields of mosaic pattern, turning portraiture and allegory into luxurious tests of surface, eros, and symbolism.

artists.name: Alphonse Mucha
artists.portraitLabel: Art Nouveau posters woven from halos and vines
artists.bio: Mucha made commercial posters feel liturgical, framing actresses and allegorical women with halos, tendrils, and curving decorative scripts.

artists.name: Henri Matisse
artists.portraitLabel: Color as structure, joy, and compression
artists.bio: Matisse uses color not as garnish but as architecture, flattening rooms, fabrics, and bodies until the entire painting pulses like a single decision.

artists.name: Pablo Picasso
artists.portraitLabel: Form broken apart and reassembled mid-look
artists.bio: Picasso keeps treating painting like an argument with its own limits, especially when faces, guitars, and tables splinter into overlapping viewpoints.

artists.name: Wassily Kandinsky
artists.portraitLabel: Abstraction as rhythm, pressure, and inner sound
artists.bio: Kandinsky treats line, color, and shape like a score, asking painting to carry emotional and spiritual resonance without depiction.

artists.name: Piet Mondrian
artists.portraitLabel: Grids reduced to primary color and balance
artists.bio: Mondrian pares painting down to black lines and primary rectangles, making equilibrium feel vivid rather than austere.

artists.name: Frida Kahlo
artists.portraitLabel: Self-portrait turned into myth, pain, and emblem
artists.bio: Kahlo turns autobiography into a dense symbolic language of bodies, plants, costumes, wounds, and stubborn frontal gaze.

artists.name: Edward Hopper
artists.portraitLabel: American rooms and streets held in uneasy pause
artists.bio: Hopper uses diners, windows, gas stations, and morning light to make ordinary American space feel psychically charged and faintly unreachable.

artists.name: Dorothea Lange
artists.portraitLabel: Documentary witness shaped by migration and labor
artists.bio: Lange frames economic crisis and displacement with an ethic of clarity, making documentary photography feel both socially exact and emotionally near.

artworks.title: Water Lilies
artworks.summary: Monet presses the lily pond close to the picture plane so reflections, blossoms, and drifting shadow read less like a vista and more like weather suspended on water.

artworks.title: Stacks of Wheat (End of Summer)
artworks.summary: Long shadows and low-angle light turn a pair of wheatstacks into a study of heat leaving the field, with color doing the work of narrative.

artworks.title: Cliff Walk at Pourville
artworks.summary: Two figures and a parasol skim the edge of the bluff while sea, grass, and sky break into brisk strokes that make the whole scene feel wind-struck.

artworks.title: The Bedroom
artworks.summary: Van Gogh painted his bedroom in the Yellow House at Arles three times. This version, created at the Saint-Rémy asylum, radiates a deceptive calm through flattened perspective and saturated color.

artworks.title: The Poet's Garden
artworks.summary: Painted at Arles, this lush garden scene was part of a decorative scheme Van Gogh planned for Paul Gauguin's room. The dense foliage and radiant greens embody his intoxication with the Provençal landscape.

artworks.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
artworks.summary: Seurat's monumental masterpiece depicts Parisians at leisure on an island in the Seine. Composed entirely of tiny dots of pure pigment, it took two years of meticulous work and redefined how color could be applied to canvas.

artworks.title: Final Study for Bathers at Asnières
artworks.summary: This intimate oil sketch captures the final compositional arrangement for Seurat's first large-scale canvas. Workers rest along the Seine at Asnières, rendered with the divided brushwork that would evolve into full pointillism.

artworks.title: The Child's Bath
artworks.summary: Cassatt's most celebrated painting shows a mother bathing her child, viewed from above in a composition influenced by Japanese woodblock prints. The bold patterns and elevated viewpoint create a tender, monumental intimacy.

artworks.title: On a Balcony
artworks.summary: A woman reads on a sunlit balcony in this early Impressionist work by Cassatt. The cropped composition and casual pose reveal her growing confidence in the radical informality championed by Degas and Manet.

artworks.title: A Camel on the Beach in Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, India
artworks.summary: Rader frames a camel and rider against a washed shoreline, making travel documentation feel lightly theatrical without losing the ordinary heat of the beach.

artworks.title: Water Pouring into a Swimming Pool
artworks.medium: Color lithograph on white wove paper
artworks.summary: A single stream of water and a hard-edged pool become a miniature manifesto for Hockney's belief that leisure could be as graphically arresting as any billboard.

artworks.title: Cushions
artworks.medium: Etching and aquatint on white wove paper
artworks.summary: Hockney turns a pile of pillows into an argument for flat color, surface pleasure, and the sly theatricality of domestic things.

artworks.title: The Artist Is Present
artworks.summary: A seated encounter stripped of almost everything but looking becomes emblematic through its documentary still: attention held long enough to feel architectural.

artworks.title: Head of a Roebuck and Two Ptarmigan
artworks.summary: Landseer makes a hunting still life feel startlingly intimate, turning fur and feather into a lesson in attention rather than trophy display.

artworks.title: Wounded Stag and Dog
artworks.summary: The scene stages sympathy, pursuit, and exhaustion all at once, showing how Landseer could make sporting art read like melodrama.

artworks.title: 1920 - Before the Storm
artworks.summary: Rozalski lets mist, uniforms, and a hulking machine share the same weather, so the alternate history arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as plot.

artworks.title: Chaos, No. 2
artworks.summary: Hilma af Klint turns abstract painting into a charged diagram, where curving forms and disciplined color feel half botanical, half occult.

artworks.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
artworks.summary: Bosch packs paradise, appetite, and punishment into one impossible panorama, making every corner of the triptych feel like a fresh outbreak of invention.

artworks.title: Les Andelys, Côte d'Aval
artworks.summary: Signac turns a riverside bluff into a slow shimmer of divided color, making geology and atmosphere feel equally provisional.

exhibitions.title: Light & Color: The Impressionist Revolution
exhibitions.description: A sweeping survey of how Impressionist painters dismantled academic convention through plein-air technique, broken color, and radical subject matter drawn from modern life.

exhibitions.title: Beyond the Dot: Seurat, Van Gogh, and Post-Impressionism
exhibitions.description: From Seurat's optical science to Van Gogh's emotional intensity, this exhibition traces how Post-Impressionism transformed Impressionist light into something deeply personal and structurally inventive.

visits.title: Saturday at the Art Institute
visits.notes: Spent the afternoon with Seurat's Grande Jatte. The scale overwhelms in person — the pointillist dots dissolve into atmosphere at the right distance.

visits.title: Morning at the Musée d'Orsay
visits.notes: The Impressionist galleries on the top floor catch the morning light through the glass ceiling. Monet's water lilies practically shimmer.

members.bio: The house notebook for launch-era reviews, lists, and museum visits while member libraries are still taking shape.
Looking for paintings that feel like stage directions for dreams.
Collecting exhibition layouts, lighting notes, and every improbable glass panel in town.

reviews.title: Monet's liquid meditation
reviews.excerpt: Standing before the water lilies, you realise Monet wasn't painting flowers — he was painting the act of seeing itself. The surface dissolves into pure color and reflection.

reviews.title: A cathedral of colored dots
reviews.excerpt: The Grande Jatte rewards patience. Stand close and you see method — tiny strokes of complementary color. Step back and a whole Sunday afternoon materialises, stiff with bourgeois composure.

reviews.title: Painting as autobiography
reviews.excerpt: Every Van Gogh canvas is a self-portrait in disguise. The bedroom, the wheat field, the night sky — each one pulses with an intensity that makes other paintings feel anemic.

reviews.title: Light itself is the subject
reviews.excerpt: The Musée d'Orsay exhibition makes a convincing case that Impressionism's real revolution wasn't subject matter but perception. Cassatt's domestic scenes hang beside Monet's landscapes with equal authority.

reviews.title: An afternoon with the Grande Jatte
reviews.excerpt: Nothing prepares you for the scale. The study panels nearby show Seurat's process — but the final canvas has a presence that no reproduction captures.

reviews.title: Where method meets feeling
reviews.excerpt: Placing Seurat's analytical pointillism next to Van Gogh's emotional impasto reveals Post-Impressionism as a dialogue between reason and passion. The AIC curators understand this tension perfectly.

lists.title: Impressionist Light
lists.description: Works that capture the fleeting magic of natural light — from Monet's haystacks to Cassatt's sunlit interiors.

lists.title: Post-Impressionist Visions
lists.description: The artists who took Impressionism's broken color and turned it into something more structural, more personal, more strange.

items.note: Pointillism at its most monumental and strange.
Intimacy through flattened perspective and pure color.

lists.title: Intimate Spaces
lists.description: Interiors, bedrooms, balconies — art that draws you into private worlds.

items.note: A room that contains an entire emotional state.
Cassatt's quiet observation of a private moment.
Workers at rest — intimacy on a riverbank.
